title: Quantinuum Processors Stand Out in Study of Quantum Error-Correction Operations
source_used: The Quantum Insider (article labelled press release about an arXiv preprint)
key_facts: A preprint on arXiv by J. A. Montañez-Barrera and Kristel Michielsen of Germany's Jülich Supercomputing Centre compared 10 processors from Quantinuum, IBM and IQM.
It proposes a benchmark based on a form of the QAOA algorithm to test the measure-and-react operations that error correction needs, before full error-correction experiments.

On IBM processors the measurement-based versions had effective error rates roughly an order of magnitude higher than versions without measurements; on Quantinuum's the extra error was comparable to that of two-qubit operations.
Quantinuum's Helios-1 scored higher at every circuit depth in a 25-data-qubit surface-code test, by two to four standard deviations per data point; a 30-qubit comparison was less conclusive.
Larger tests reached 81, 91 and 48 data qubits for three code families but did not demonstrate successful error correction at those sizes.
On IBM Phoenix, better benchmark scores generally matched fewer logical-memory errors across 11 chip areas, but only for small surface-code patches on one processor.
The paper is an arXiv preprint and not peer reviewed; the effective error rates use a simplified noise model.
quote_evidence: Quantinuum's processors handled a key step toward quantum error correction more reliably than the other machines in a new study, which also proposes a simpler way to judge whether hardware is ready for that step.
They did not demonstrate successful error correction at those sizes.
It's important to note that arXiv is a pre-print server, which allows researchers to receive quick feedback on their work.
why_it_matters_hint: A cheap way to rank hardware for error correction, with Quantinuum's machines scoring best in this study.
notes: The Quantum Insider labels the text a press release; the study itself is by independent Jülich researchers, not Quantinuum. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
